email.subject: Force majeure on Alderbrook Gathering - need your decision by 10:00
email.body:
Devrim, Florentino,

Alderbrook Gathering declared force majeure at 6:00 this morning after a compressor fire. We lose 30,000 MMBtu/d of supply starting with today's gas day. Devrim, I need you to tell me by 10:00 AM which customers to cut or where you will buy replacement gas. We cannot wait for the afternoon cycle.

Annika

email.subject: Going Forward California Costs - Future Revenue Reqts
email.body:
I wanted to make sure that everyone is on the same page related to utility costs in California.  These costs may be (will be?) collected  from some utility customer, potentially including direct access customers.


Bucket #1	Utility Undercollection Feb 1, 2000 Through Jan 18, 2001

About $12.0 Billion (this money includes our Negative CTC amounts).  Should be financed through corporate debt.  No securitization.

Enron's Position:	Bundled service on Jan 1, 2001 pays fixed c/kwh

Bucket #2	CDWR Cost from Jan 5, 2001 through Bond Issuance or March 31, 2002

About $12.5 Billion  (about $10 Billion for spot purchases and $2.5 Billion for long-term buys)

Enron's Position:	Dedicated Rate Component (DRC) for all residential and small customers.  Larger customers are assigned direct responsibility for the Undercollection on c/kwh.  Balancing account for holding Utility even.  

Bucket #3	Prospective Generation Costs for Bundled Service Post March 31, 2002

URG 	= $40/mwh (retained generation and bilateral contracts)
CDWR 	= $120/mwh
QF 	= $100/mwh  

TOTAL 	= URG*%sales + CDWR*%sales + QF*%sales
	= $90/mwh


Bucket #4	AB1890 Non-Generation Stranded Costs



Bucket #5	AB1890 Generation Stranded Costs

email.subject: well....
email.body:
I can't imagine the volume of fan mail on your exit, so I'll be brief. 
Just returned from an unplugged vacation to read the surprising/intriguing news.  3 comments: 
1.  The Times tells me you're engaged.  A thousand blessings on your heads.  (I always wished I were Jewish but couldn't qualify on taste or IQ).
2.  I've told people that  you are my business hero for several years now.  It seems a little unfair that you would now vie for the "personal life" hero as well, so I'll hold that title in abeyance for the moment. It goes without saying that if there were ever any way to work together, the firm (not that firm) and I would be honored.
3.  On the trip back, I've been reading Katharine Graham's autobiography.   Apparently, she slept a lot with Adlai Stevenson, another wicked smart guy.  His most widely used quote at "retirement":
"I'd just like to lie under a tree with a glass of wine and watch people dance." 
They say he was too smart to be President. 
All the best. 
jt 
John Thornton 
General Partner 
Austin Ventures 
512.485.1904

email.subject: Rating Changes to COI, PDCI, Path 15 and 26 for 8/21/01
email.body:
Market Notification: After the Day Ahead Market ran for 8/21/01, the COI
Branch Group (Path 66) limit was changed from 4030 to 4000 MW (N-S) and from
2450 to 3675 MW (S-N) for HE01 through HE06.  From HE07 through HE16 (N-S),
Path 66 was changed from 4030 to 4300 MW and from 2450 to 3675 MW (S-N). In
addition, the NOB Branch Group (Path 65) the S-N was changed from 2525 to
2875 MW and S-N was changed from 1904 to 2084 MW.  Path 15 (N-S) was changed
from 1275 to 1100 MW and Path 26 (N-S) 3000 MW to 2500 MW.  Path 15 and 26
in the South-North directions will remain as pre-scheduled. This is due to
the Los Banos-Gates Line Series cap being removed from service.  The first
applicable hour to submit adjusted schedules in the Hour-Ahead market is
HE03.  Please address real-time operational inquiries to the Real Time
scheduling desk at (916) 351-2493, sent by Market Operations (916) 351-4409.

With the daily chaos that ensues on this floor, sometimes communication is sacrificed.  Fortunately, we have the message board to facilitate real time sharing of information.  I think all of us, including myself, underutilize this tool.  I want to encourage everybody to keep the board open on their computers all day long.  In addition, I want everybody to post at least one message every day.  This can be an interesting trade that just happened, what counterparties are trying to do, new information you uncovered, etc.  Information we learn can be very valuable to other desks and it is only fair that if we're taking info from the board, we should be contributing as well.

email.body: Jean,  I have reviewed Marathon's revisions to the CA.  I agree that these changes are minor and I am OK with all of them except one.  With respect to the stricken sentence in Paragraph 7, I would ask Marathon the reason for the strike.  I think the sentence only reinforces the right to compete concept in the first sentence and further specify's the concept.  I would be happy to discuss this further with Marathon.  Thanks.

Steve,

I need your help with something.  I want to look at Pasadena's load profile and am having trouble obtaining this.  Is it possible for you to send me your actual daily burns for up to the past two years?  This would be helpful in assisting you with your risk management needs and with structuring products specifically for Pasadena.

Let me know if you can help.

Thanks,

Kim

email.subject: West Coast Power Matters
email.body:
Per our conversation yesterday, I propose we send out the following memo:

In order to better coordinate the various west coast power matters, effective immediately, Jim Steffes and Richard Sanders will jointly take the lead role.  Jim and Richard will be responsible for preparing a comphrehensive strategy for all the matters, reviewing the strategy with the California Committee and seeking approval of the California Committee before taking any material action.  Please do all you can to assist Jim and Richard on the west coast power matters.

I would copy only the people working on these matters including Steffes, Sanders, Belden, Mellencamp, Shapiro, Sharp, Williams, Tribolet, Lavorato and Delainey.
